scope: Theorem 10.7 (A guarded processor in a fixed torus chart) of the manuscript “Incompressible Box Transport and Finite Computation” (preprints/Incompressible-Box-Transport-and-Finite-Computation-October-6-2026/manuscript.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 376 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 2505dc09d3f2c24b), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 39. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For each machine and finite input, at any fixed positive computable viscosity there is an effective smooth mean-zero force on the unit flat three-torus, with bounded mixed derivatives and period one for t ≥ 1, whose smooth zero-data solution has pressure zero and satisfies ∃t ≥ 0 : X(t; [(−1/16, 0, 0)]) ∈ {[x] : x1 mod 1 ∈ (0, 1/2)} ⇐⇒ the machine halts. The pressure is normalized to mean zero, and the solution is unique in the classical torus comparison class of Section 2.
